A session with me

Live and unhurried

Here is everything, start to finish.

Getting a session

  1. 1

    Tap Wish at the bottom of the screen. Choose to see me, or to only hear me.

  2. 2

    Tap the button to ask. I am told the moment you do, and I answer from my side.

  3. 3

    When I say yes, a gold card appears at the top of the Wish page. That card is how you will know — nothing else is needed.

  4. 4

    Tap Pick your time on it and choose any day and time that suits you, up to a month ahead.

Arriving

  1. 1

    I will remind you as the day comes closer — on your phone, not only in the app.

  2. 2

    On the day, open Ivory about five minutes early. Nobody rings your phone. You come here.

  3. 3

    Tap Wish, tap your session, tap Join. If it says you are early, close it and tap Join again in a few minutes.

  4. 4

    Then wait. I come in from my side, and the screen tells you the moment I do.

Good to know

  1. 1

    The clock starts when we are actually connected — never at the hour on the card.

  2. 2

    If you lose the app, come straight back and tap Join again. Your place is held.

  3. 3

    If we are still talking when the time runs out, I can offer you more. You will see it on your screen, and it is yours to refuse.

  4. 4

    Something came up? Ask me to move it and I will. You will find me in the quiet door on your Profile page.

      the fine print

      privacy, safety & terms

      Nothing hidden, nothing shouted.

      Four short documents — what this house is, what it does with what you tell it, what it promises, and what comes back if something goes wrong. Written in plain sentences, and the same words the app keeps.

      the officer · the quiet door

      Every complaint, question or legal notice reaches a person, not a queue. Write to the Grievance Officer named here and it is answered — there is no script and no ticket tree behind it.

      Grievance OfficerIndrani Chakraverty

      48 hoursto acknowledge
      your complaint
      one monthto resolve it
      or say why not
      same dayfor anything
      about safety
      On the web. This page sets no advertising cookie, carries no tracking pixel, and loads nothing from anyone else — with one exception, named here: when you choose to pay by card, the payment window itself is Razorpay’s, the same house your payments already go through in the app. Until you tap pay, nothing of theirs is loaded. There are two ways to settle anything: by UPI, where the money leaves your bank for the house’s own id and you send the reference so it can be checked against the statement by hand; or by card and netbanking through Razorpay. The house may have one of them resting at any time, and the page you pay on only ever offers the one it has open. Card details never reach Ivory on either road — they are typed into the payment window and stay with Razorpay and your bank. The only other thing this site stores is your own preference — sound, a remembered visit — and that stays in your browser. The two clocks above are the ones India’s consumer rules ask for; the safety line moves faster than either.

      Ivory · the fine print · 2026

      the fine print

      Content & conduct

      Last updated 2026 · the same words as the app

      01What Ivory is

      Stories, voice, film and private conversation, made by one artist. Intimate in tone, adult in audience, and suggestive where it wants to be.

      02What Ivory is not

      No nudity. No sexual acts, shown or described in explicit detail. No in-person meetings, arranged or hinted at, ever. No escorting, no soliciting, and nothing that treats a member as a transaction.

      These are not temporary limits. They are what the house is.

      03Adults only

      Every member confirms they are 18 or older. The app is rated for adults. An account found to belong to someone younger is closed and refunded.

      04How members behave

      Be decent. Do not demand what section 2 says does not exist. Do not press for a personal number, an address or a meeting. Do not record. Do not repeat a private conversation outside Ivory.

      A member who harasses or threatens is removed immediately and without refund. There is no second warning for that one.

      05How the house behaves

      The house will never ask for your password, your card number, your UPI PIN or an OTP. The house will never ask you to pay anywhere outside the app. The house will never propose meeting you.

      If a message appears to come from Ivory and does any of those things, it is not from Ivory. Report it through the quiet door.

      06What happens in a session

      A session is between the two people in it. The house does not record. You may not record. Either side may end a session at any moment, for any reason or none.

      07Reporting

      The quiet door is on the privacy, safety and terms page and inside the app wherever something can go wrong. It reaches a person, not a queue, and the serious things are dealt with the same day.

      08If something unlawful appears

      Tell the house. It is removed on sight, the account behind it is closed, and where the law requires it the matter is reported to the authorities.

      09AI and authenticity

      Everything in Ivory is made by the artist. Nothing here is a synthetic likeness of another person, and nothing is presented as someone it is not.

      the fine print

      Privacy

      Last updated 2026 · the same words as the app

      01The short version

      Ivory collects as little as it can get away with. Nothing is sold. Nothing is handed to advertisers. There are no tracking pixels and no advertising networks anywhere in this app.

      02What is collected

      Your account: the email address you use to sign in and the name you choose to show. At signup you may also provide an optional phone number and date of birth. Those details are kept apart from your public profile and are not shown to other members.

      Your profile photo, if you choose one. It appears on your Profile page and beside your messages in live chat. Only people allowed to view that broadcast can view the chat photo. If you are a confirmed gifter on a post, your photo also appears beside your name in that post's gifts section, visible only to members who can open that post.

      Your membership: which tier you hold, when it started and when it renews.

      Your payments: the amount, the date, the reference number you type in after paying, and the screenshot if you send one. The house never sees your card, your bank login or your UPI PIN - those stay with your own bank and payment app.

      Your activity in Ivory: what you have unlocked, which sessions you have booked, how long a session lasted, and the messages you send to the house.

      Your Quiet Folio, if you use it: private notes, writing drafts, saved web links and optional notes linked to your own scheduled calls. These entries sync to your Ivory account so you can return to them on another device. They are not end-to-end encrypted.

      Your device, for notifications only: a token from Google that lets a message reach your phone. It identifies the phone, not you, and it is deleted when you sign out.

      03What is not collected

      No location. No contacts. No browsing of other apps. The app reads only the photo you deliberately choose for your profile; it does not scan your photo library. No microphone or camera except during a session you joined yourself, and nothing from them is recorded or stored. No advertising identifier.

      04Why

      To let you in, to show you what your membership includes, to run the sessions you book, to confirm payments, to answer you when you write, to keep the private Folio pages you choose to save, and to meet the record-keeping the law requires of anyone taking money. A phone number is optional, is not a sign-in method, and is not displayed publicly. If you share your real birthday, Ivory will try to prepare a small birthday token; it is not guaranteed.

      05Who else sees it

      Supabase holds sign-in, the database and private profile-photo files; Google Firebase delivers notifications; Agora carries the live audio and video; Cloudflare R2 stores film, voice and published post photo/cover files; Razorpay, where used, handles payment. Each receives only what is needed to make that service work.

      Published post photos and covers use public image links; only publish images intended to be visible to anyone with their link. Profile photos and payment screenshots stay on a private path and use time-limited viewing links.

      The Ivory house can access optional phone and birthday details for account administration and the possible birthday token. Other members cannot see those details. A member who is allowed to view the same live broadcast can see your chat messages and, if you chose a photo, that photo beside them. Photo files are private; the app uses time-limited links to display them. Anyone given such a link may view it until it expires.

      Quiet Folio pages are protected by database rules tied to your signed-in account; other members and the app's ordinary admin screens cannot read them. They are not end-to-end encrypted. Authorized service operators with privileged database access may access account data where needed to operate or support the service.

      No advertiser or data broker receives your information. The only other exception is a demand the house is legally required to answer, and the house will tell you if that happens unless forbidden.

      06Calls are not recorded

      Sessions are live only. No recording is made by the house, not of video, not of audio. What was said exists only in the memory of the two people who were there. Recording a session yourself is forbidden by the terms of use.

      07How long it is kept

      Your account details stay while the account exists. Optional phone and birthday details are stored separately from the public profile. Quiet Folio entries stay until you delete them or ask for account erasure. Profile photos stay until you remove or replace them, or ask for erasure. Payment records are kept for eight years because tax law requires it. Messages to the house are kept while the matter is open and for a reasonable time after. Notification tokens die when you sign out. Nothing is auto-deleted behind your back.

      08Your rights

      You may view, edit or delete each Quiet Folio page in the app. You may also ask what is held about you, ask for a mistake to be corrected, ask for your account and its data to be erased, and withdraw a consent you gave. Ask through the quiet door or write to the Grievance Officer. The house answers within 30 days, and usually the same day.

      Erasure removes what the law allows to be removed. Payment records stay for the eight years mentioned above - the house is not permitted to delete those.

      09Children

      Ivory is for adults. The house does not knowingly hold the data of anyone under 18, and deletes it on discovery.

      10Security

      Everything travels encrypted. Access to the database is restricted by rules that run on the server, not in the app, so one member cannot read another's private account details. No system is beyond failure; if one happens and it affects you, the house will tell you and tell the authorities, as the law requires.

      11Where it lives

      Data is stored on servers operated by the providers in section 5, which may be outside India. They are bound to protect it to the standard described here.

      12Changes

      If this notice changes, the date at the top changes and the app says so.

      13Who to ask

      The Grievance Officer named on the privacy, safety and terms page. A real person, and the only address the house uses for this.

      the fine print

      Terms of use

      Last updated 2026 · the same words as the app

      01Who this is between

      Ivory is run by one person, from India. In these terms "the house" means Ivory, and "you" means the member reading them. Using the app means you accept what is written here. If you do not, please stop using it and ask for your account to be removed through the quiet door.

      02You must be 18

      Ivory is for adults only. By using it you confirm you are 18 years old or more. If the house has reason to believe a member is under 18, the account is closed and anything paid for and not yet delivered is refunded.

      03What Ivory is

      Ivory is a private place for stories, voice, film and conversation made by one artist for the people who choose to be here. There is no nudity and no explicit content. There are no meetings in person, ever, and nobody from the house will suggest one.

      04Your account

      Your account is yours alone. Do not share the login. If you think someone else has reached it, tell the house immediately through the quiet door and it will be locked while it is sorted out.

      05What you may not do

      Do not record, screenshot, copy, repost or sell anything you see or hear in Ivory. Do not quote a private session anywhere outside it. Do not use Ivory to harass anyone, to threaten anyone, or to pass anything unlawful through it. Do not try to break, probe or overload the app or the services behind it.

      Any of these can end a membership without a refund of time already used.

      06Membership and payment

      Tiers are paid in advance for a stated period. What each tier includes is shown on the membership page before you pay and can change for future periods, never for one already paid for. Prices are in Indian rupees and include any tax the house is required to collect.

      07Sessions

      A session is a private call booked inside Ivory. A booking needs a free slot, and slots exist only inside the hours shown on the calendar. Sessions start when both sides connect, not at the clock time. Running past the booked length does not end a session; the house may offer more time, at a price shown before you agree to it.

      If you cannot make a session, move it. The reschedule button is there for exactly that and there is no charge for using it.

      08If the house cannot attend

      If a session cannot happen from the house's side, it is rescheduled at your convenience or refunded in full, whichever you prefer. That is a promise, not a courtesy.

      09Content belongs to the house

      Everything in Ivory - words, voice, film, photographs, the look of the app - belongs to the house. Paying for access is paying to see and hear it, here, for as long as your access lasts. It is not a transfer of ownership and it is not permission to use it anywhere else.

      10What you send

      Anything you write or send to the house stays yours. By sending it you allow the house to read it, keep it while it is needed, and answer it. The house will not publish anything you sent privately.

      11When things break

      Ivory is run honestly and carefully, but no app is perfect. The house does not promise it will never be unavailable. Where the law allows, the house's responsibility for any one problem is limited to what you paid for the thing that went wrong. Nothing here removes a right you have under Indian consumer law.

      12Ending it

      You may stop being a member whenever you like; access runs to the end of the period you have paid for. The house may close an account that breaks section 5, or that is used to harm another member.

      13The law

      These terms are governed by the law of India, and the courts of West Bengal have jurisdiction. If any single sentence here is found unenforceable, the rest still stands.

      14Changes

      If these terms change, the date at the top changes and the app will say so. Continuing to use Ivory after that means you accept the new version.

      15Reaching a person

      Every complaint, question or legal notice goes to the Grievance Officer named on the previous page, or through the quiet door inside the app. A real person reads it.

      the fine print

      Refunds

      Last updated 2026 · the same words as the app

      01The idea

      A purchase in Ivory is a ticket to a private performance. The moment it reaches you it has been performed, so a change of mind is not a refund. That is the rule, and the exceptions below are real exceptions, not loopholes to argue through.

      02Always refunded

      A ticket that never arrived. You paid and nothing unlocked, or it unlocked and will not open.

      A double charge. Two payments for one thing, whatever caused it.

      A show pulled before you stepped in. You paid for something that was then taken down before you could see or hear it.

      A session the house could not attend. Full refund, or a new time, whichever you prefer.

      03Sessions

      A session you cannot make should be moved, not cancelled. The reschedule button is on the session itself and costs nothing.

      If you simply do not come, and do not move it, the time is used. The house held that hour for you and turned others away. After a small number of no-shows the booking privilege pauses; the app tells you where you stand before that happens.

      A session cut short by a failure on the house's side is either finished later at your convenience or refunded for the part you did not get.

      04Membership

      A tier is paid for a period and runs to the end of that period. Stopping a membership stops the next renewal; it does not refund the period you are inside. If a tier is charged after you stopped it, that is a double charge under section 2 and it comes back.

      05Extensions

      Time added to a session that then could not be used, because of a failure on the house's side, is refunded in full.

      06How to ask

      Use the quiet door inside the app and choose "a payment or refund". Tell the house what happened and quote the reference number from your payment. Ask within the window shown on the privacy, safety and terms page.

      07What happens next

      The house replies, and serious things are dealt with the same day. An approved refund goes back to the method you paid from, within the number of days shown on that same page. The house cannot send it anywhere else - that is a rule of the payment system, not a preference.

      08If you are not satisfied

      Write to the Grievance Officer. If you are still not satisfied, nothing here takes away your right to go to a consumer forum under the Consumer Protection Act 2019.
